channel.title: Global Competition Review - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Global Competition Review (globalcompetitionreview.com)

item.title: Call for reinforcements: The Tipline for 23 February 2026
item.description: The Department of Justice is hiring. The Antitrust Division listed 14 job openings on Monday for attorneys to work on civil and criminal matters in Chicago, San Francisco and Washington, DC. Meanwhile, Live Nation continues its push to scrap the division’s monopolisation suit, arguing that last week’s summary judgment order spoils what remains of the case.

item.title: UGG maker hit with monopolisation suit
item.description: The manufacturer of UGG boots weaponised hundreds of “sham” trade dress lawsuits to exclude competition and maintain supracompetitive prices, a rival footwear manufacturer has alleged.

item.title: US enforcers drafting collaboration guidelines
item.description: The US antitrust agencies have requested public input on new guidelines outlining permissible collaboration between competitors, following the Biden Administration's withdrawal of the previous document in 2024.

item.title: Push back: The Briefing for 24 February 2026
item.description: Israeli flag carrier El Al faces a potential €30 million abuse of dominance fine after allegedly blocking its main rival from accessing its hangar facilities. This exposed Arkia to the threat of consumer lawsuits amid potential flight delays and cancellations, the country’s competition watchdog has warned in a statement of objections. item.title: Google’s approach to disclosure is “deficient”, Epic Games says
item.description: The UK’s Competition Appeal Tribunal should “draw a line” under a disclosure dispute between Epic Games and Google by setting the search parameters the tech company should use to locate material potentially relevant to the lawsuit, the gaming company has said.

item.title: Gurr: “Judge me on the track record”
item.description: Doug Gurr has stopped short of promising to recuse himself from any decision to designate Amazon under the UK’s digital competition regime, while assuring lawmakers that he is ready to become permanent chair at the antitrust agency.

item.title: Interim measures ruling incoming in first challenge against German sector inquiry “call-in” order
item.description: Remondis expects a German appellate court to rule within the coming days on an interim injunction application to suspend the Federal Cartel Office’s use of new sector inquiry powers to force the business to notify future acquisitions.

item.title: The heart of it all: The Tipline for 24 February 2026
item.description: Ohio attorney general David Yost is continuing his antitrust push. Following a complaint against cannabis companies and a suit against Ohio Health with the Department of Justice, the Buckeye State has now brought criminal bid-rigging charges. “Going once, going twice – going to court!” Yost said on Tuesday. Also in Tipline, Warner Bros Discovery says Paramount’s newest bid may be the best offer.&n...

item.title: News outlets claim FTC probe threatens journalism
item.description: The Federal Trade Commission’s investigation of Media Matters targeted “quintessential” press activity protected by the First Amendment, according to several news outlets, including The New York Times and The Associated Press.

item.title: Agri Stats case ready for trial, judge says
item.description: The Department of Justice may proceed with its claims that Agri Stats operated an illegal information exchange to inflate prices for chicken, pig and cow products across the US, a Minnesota federal court has ruled.
